correctness.rationale: Theorem 7.1 of arXiv:2611.16283v1 supplies nonnegative coefficients, degree n² and top coefficient 1/n for each a_n(q). Thus q^(n²)/n<=a_n(q)<=q^(n²)a_n(1). The q=1 branch equals 1+x A+x A² and evaluates to 2 at x=1/6, so a_n(1)<=2*6^n. The n² coefficient growth is a consequence of these exact inequalities. Standard algebraic-series convergence and factorial-polynomial ceilings for P-recursive sequences give radius-zero, transcendence and nonholonomicity. Exponent and normalization boundaries, q=0,1 and each fixed integer q>=2 have been checked.
